about.title: Vacaville Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A wet floor without a cone, a parking-lot pothole that never got patched, a stairway with a loose handrail — falls like these happen in Vacaville every week, in the retail areas off Nut Tree Road, along the business stretches of Alamo Drive and Peabody Road, and in apartment complexes across town. Under California law, the property owner isn't automatically responsible just because you fell. You generally have to show they knew about the hazard, or reasonably should have known, and did nothing to fix it or warn you. That's called notice, and it's where most of these cases are won or lost. Evidence disappears fast. Store video is often overwritten within days, spills get mopped, and broken steps get repaired. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Vacaville residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Solano County premises cases and works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. You focus on healing; the attorney handles the investigation.

whyChoose.title: Why Vacaville Fall Victims Use LawProactive

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Real Investigation
items.desc: California asks you to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorney you're connected with can pursue inspection logs, cleaning schedules and prior complaints that establish it.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many Vacaville stores and complexes keep footage only briefly before it's recorded over. An attorney can send a preservation demand quickly so the video showing your fall isn't lost.

items.title: The Clock and Comparative Fault Both Matter
items.desc: You typically have two years to file, but far less if a public entity owns the property. And because California uses pure comparative fault, even a partial share of blame doesn't erase your claim — it reduces it.

items.question: I fell at a park or on a sidewalk owned by the City of Vacaville. Is the process different?
items.answer: Yes, and the timing is much tighter. Claims against a California city, county or other public entity generally require a formal government claim within six months of the injury, well before the two-year deadline that applies to private property. Missing that window can end the case before it starts. Talk to an attorney early if the City of Vacaville or Solano County may be involved.

items.question: The store says I should have been watching where I walked. Do I still have a case?
items.answer: Possibly. California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery is reduced by whatever percentage of blame is assigned to you rather than eliminated entirely. If a jury decided you were 20 percent at fault, you would still be able to recover the other 80 percent. An attorney can evaluate how strong the owner's argument really is.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall in Vacaville?
items.answer: Photograph the hazard from several angles before it's cleaned up or repaired, and get names of anyone who saw you fall. Ask the business for an incident report and request in writing that they preserve any camera footage. See a doctor even if you feel mostly okay, since hip and head injuries can surface later. Then reach out, and LawProactive will connect you with an independent attorney at no cost.
